prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an outdoor walkway bordered by a storefront wall and counter on the left (1–3 m away), a continuous ground plane beneath, and an open parking area on the right receding beyond 10 m. Across the five frames, as the camera wearer pans left in frame 2, pans right toward the parking lot in frame 4, and returns to center in frame 5, two foreground companions stay within or near arm's reach: a person in a red shirt on the left at roughly 0.6–1.2 m (partially cropped at the left edge in frames 1 and 5, centered in frame 2, and out of view in frames 3–4) and a woman in a black top with crossed arms at 0.8–1.5 m (about 0.8–1.0 m right of the red-shirted person, facing and looking toward the camera wearer, and cropped at the lower-left edge in frame 4). Further down the walkway behind the foreground woman, two distant pedestrians stand 1–2 m apart at roughly 6–10 m in frames 1 and 3–5, while frame 4 reveals two people standing side by side within arm's reach of each other at 2.5–3.5 m in front of parked cars at 4–8 m. Compared to the motion-blurred, high-contrast nighttime RGB strip, the depth map much more clearly separates the foreground silhouettes, ground slope, and mid-range parked cars from the dark background. However, the depth map is unreliable around the glass storefront in frame 2—where interior shelves and people 3–5 m inside blend ambiguously with the window plane—and along the blurred left shoulder in frame 5 where depth values saturate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels discrete people, vehicles, handbags, and elevated store displays across the walkway scene as the camera wearer turns left in frame 2, right in frame 4, and back to center in frame 5. In the foreground at 0.6–1.5 m (within or near arm's reach of the camera wearer and about 1 m from each other), it segments the red-shirted person on the left in frames 1–2 (plus their backpack strap as a handbag within arm's reach in frame 1) and the woman in black facing the camera wearer across frames 1–5, though her mask is heavily cropped at the bottom-left boundary in frame 4 and the red-shirted person is completely missed on the far left of frame 5. In the background of frames 1 and 3–5, it isolates the two pedestrians 6–10 m ahead down the corridor (standing 1–2 m apart, with a handbag segmented on the right person in frame 1), while frame 2 segments two overhead TV monitors and distant people 3–5 m inside the store to the left. As the camera pans right in frame 3 and 4, the map captures two people standing side by side at 2.5–3.5 m (facing left toward the walkway and partially occluding the cars behind them) along with multiple parked cars at 3–8 m. While segmentation makes small, motion-blurred background pedestrians, distant cars, and store monitors much easier to spot than in the RGB strip alone, it is unreliable when misclassifying backpack straps as handbags, fragmenting overlapping cars in frames 3–4, and missing the cropped person on the left edge of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks 2D upper-body skeletal keypoints and facial landmarks only for the closest foreground individuals standing 1.0–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer, leaving the background walkway, storefront, and parking lot completely blank. In frame 1, it renders the head and right shoulder-to-wrist arm segment of the woman in black facing and looking toward the camera wearer, and in frame 2—as the camera wearer turns left—it shifts to the head and both shoulders/upper arms of the red-shirted person at roughly 1.2 m facing the camera wearer while missing the woman in black partially visible on the right. In frames 3 and 4, as the camera wearer turns right with motion blur and partial cropping at the frame edges, all people—including the woman in black within arm's reach at the bottom-left and the pedestrians 2.5–10 m away—are completely absent from the pose map. In frame 5, when the camera returns to the center, the woman in black at ~1.2 m is detected again with facial keypoints looking toward the camera wearer, a full torso box, and crossed forearms within her own reach, while the partially visible person at the left edge (~0.7 m) and distant pedestrians (~7–10 m) remain undetected. The pose map clarifies the exact shoulder orientation and crossed-arm geometry against the dark clothing in frame 5 that is hard to discern in RGB, but it is highly unreliable under motion blur, occlusion, and distance, failing to detect any hand skeletons (magenta) across all five frames and dropping all bodies in frames 3 and 4.
